title: The derived square isomorphism commutes with the shift isomorphisms of the inverse images
statement:
Let $\square=(f,f',g,g',\alpha)$ be a cartesian square of schemes [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], with $f:X	o Y$, $g:Y'	o Y$, $f':X'	o Y'$, $g':X'	o X$, and let $	heta^D_\square:f'^{-1}g^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}g'^{-1}f^{-1}$ be the derived square isomorphism of functors $\Dplus(Y_{\Et})	o\Dplus(X'_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-square-iso]. Give each inverse image $u^{-1}$ on bounded below derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image] its shift-commutation isomorphism $\iota^u_M:u^{-1}(M[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}(u^{-1}M)[1]$, the identity of the termwise shifted complex $u^{-1}(M^ ullet[1])=(u^{-1}M^ ullet)[1]$ on a representing complex ($(M[1])^r=M^{r+1}$, $d_{M[1]}=-d_M$), and give the composites $f'^{-1}g^{-1}$ and $g'^{-1}f^{-1}$ the composite isomorphisms $\varphi_M=\iota^{f'}_{g^{-1}M}\circ f'^{-1}(\iota^g_M)$ and $\psi_M=\iota^{g'}_{f^{-1}M}\circ g'^{-1}(\iota^f_M)$ [lem-weil-pbc-triangulated-functor-composite]. Then for every $M\in\Dplus(Y_{\Et})$
$$
 \psi_M\circ	heta^D_{\square,M[1]}=	heta^D_{\square,M}[1]\circ\varphi_M:\ f'^{-1}g^{-1}(M[1])\longrightarrow(g'^{-1}f^{-1}M)[1],
$$
and hence the same holds for the iterated isomorphisms $\varphi^{(n)},\psi^{(n)}$ and the shifts $[n]$, $n\in\mathbf Z$.

source.place: Definition 014V (definition-exact-functor-triangulated-categories, line 191) and Lemma 05SU (lemma-derived-shift, line 4657: compatibility of derived functors with shifts); the inverse images act termwise on complexes and their shift isomorphisms are identities of termwise shifted complexes. The statement is assembled by an agent: Stacks uses the compatibility without stating it. Proof places: Proposition 05R6 (line 1360) and Definition 05RU (line 3690) of derived.tex for the exact localization Q and the shift on D(A); homology.tex Definition 011G (line 3427) for the shift of complexes; categories.tex Lemma 04VG (line 4406) clause (3) for uniqueness through Q.

proof.text:
**Step 1 (notation; the shift compatibility of the identifications $\beta$).** Work first on the unbounded derived categories. For $u\in\{f,g,f',g'\}$ let $u^{-1}_D$ be the functor on $D$ induced termwise, $\beta_u:u^{-1}_D\circ Q\xrightarrow{\sim}Q\circ u^{-1}$ its identification and $\iota^u_X:u^{-1}_D(X[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}u^{-1}_D(X)[1]$ ($X\in D$) its shift isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image]; let $c_K:Q(K[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}(QK)[1]$ be the shift isomorphism of the exact functor $Q$, natural in the complex $K$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The termwise functor $u^{-1}$ on complexes satisfies $u^{-1}(K[1])=(u^{-1}K)[1]$ literally (degree $r$: $u^{-1}K^{r+1}$; differential $u^{-1}(-d^{r+1})=-u^{-1}d^{r+1}$, $u^{-1}$ being additive), with the identity as shift isomorphism. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] for $F=u^{-1}$, $n=1$, $\tau=\mathrm{id}$ reads: for every complex $K$
$$\beta_{u,K}[1]\circ\iota^u_{QK}\circ u^{-1}_D(c_K)=c_{u^{-1}K}\circ\beta_{u,K[1]}:\ u^{-1}_D(Q(K[1]))\to(Q(u^{-1}K))[1],\qquad(\ast_u)$$
i.e. $\beta_u$ is compatible with the shift, $u^{-1}_D\circ Q$ carrying the composite isomorphism $\iota^u_Q\circ u^{-1}_D(c)$ and $Q\circ u^{-1}$ the composite $c_{u^{-1}}\circ Q(\mathrm{id})$ [lem-weil-pbc-triangulated-functor-composite].

Written out by an agent: Stacks uses the compatibility without stating it.

proof.text: **Step 2 (the composite identifications $\beta_1,\beta_2$ are compatible with the shift).** Let $\beta_1=\beta_{f',g^{-1}K}\circ f'^{-1}_D(\beta_{g,K})$ and $\beta_2=\beta_{g',f^{-1}K}\circ g'^{-1}_D(\beta_{f,K})$ be the identifications of [def-weil-pbc-derived-square-iso], and $\varphi_X=\iota^{f'}_{g^{-1}_DX}\circ f'^{-1}_D(\iota^g_X)$, $\psi_X=\iota^{g'}_{f^{-1}_DX}\circ g'^{-1}_D(\iota^f_X)$ the composite shift isomorphisms of the statement (on $D$). Claim: $\beta_{1,K}[1]\circ\varphi_{QK}\circ f'^{-1}_Dg^{-1}_D(c_K)=c_{f'^{-1}g^{-1}K}\circ\beta_{1,K[1]}$, and the same with $\beta_2,\psi$, $g'^{-1}f^{-1}$. This is [lem-weil-pbc-commshift-nattrans-comp-whisker] (ii) (whisker $\beta_g$ by $f'^{-1}_D$), (iii) (whisker $\beta_{f'}$ by the termwise $g^{-1}$, whose shift isomorphism is the identity) and (i) (compose). Written out: $\beta_{1,K}[1]\circ\varphi_{QK}\circ f'^{-1}_Dg^{-1}_D(c_K)=\beta_{f',g^{-1}K}[1]\circ f'^{-1}_D(\beta_{g,K})[1]\circ\iota^{f'}_{g^{-1}_DQK}\circ f'^{-1}_D(\iota^g_{QK}\circ g^{-1}_D(c_K))$; naturality of $\iota^{f'}$ for the morphism $\beta_{g,K}$ moves $f'^{-1}_D(\beta_{g,K})[1]\circ\iota^{f'}_{g^{-1}_DQK}$ to $\iota^{f'}_{Q(g^{-1}K)}\circ f'^{-1}_D(\beta_{g,K}[1])$; then $(\ast_g)$ inside $f'^{-1}_D$ turns $f'^{-1}_D(\beta_{g,K}[1]\circ\iota^g_{QK}\circ g^{-1}_D(c_K))$ into $f'^{-1}_D(c_{g^{-1}K})\circ f'^{-1}_D(\beta_{g,K[1]})$; and $(\ast_{f'})$ at the complex $g^{-1}K$ turns $\beta_{f',g^{-1}K}[1]\circ\iota^{f'}_{Q(g^{-1}K)}\circ f'^{-1}_D(c_{g^{-1}K})$ into $c_{f'^{-1}g^{-1}K}\circ\beta_{f',g^{-1}(K[1])}$, using $g^{-1}(K[1])=(g^{-1}K)[1]$. The result is $c_{f'^{-1}g^{-1}K}\circ\beta_{f',g^{-1}(K[1])}\circ f'^{-1}_D(\beta_{g,K[1]})=c_{f'^{-1}g^{-1}K}\circ\beta_{1,K[1]}$. Same computation for $\beta_2$.

proof.text: **Step 3 (the termwise $\theta$ commutes with the shift of complexes).** For a complex $K$ on $Y_{\Et}$, the termwise isomorphism $\theta_{\square,K[1]}:f'^{-1}g^{-1}(K[1])\to g'^{-1}f^{-1}(K[1])$ and the shifted isomorphism $\theta_{\square,K}[1]:(f'^{-1}g^{-1}K)[1]\to(g'^{-1}f^{-1}K)[1]$ are the same morphism of complexes: source and target agree literally (Step 1), and in degree $r$ both are $\theta_{\square,K^{r+1}}$ (homology.tex 011G: $f[1]^r=f^{r+1}$; the sign of the differential plays no role in the components). Hence the shift isomorphisms of the termwise composites (identities) are respected by $\theta_{\square,-}$, and by naturality of $c$ for the morphism $\theta_{\square,K}$: $c_{g'^{-1}f^{-1}K}\circ Q(\theta_{\square,K[1]})=(Q\theta_{\square,K})[1]\circ c_{f'^{-1}g^{-1}K}$.

**Step 4 (the square on the image of $Q$).** Let $\theta^D_{\mathrm{unb}}:f'^{-1}_Dg^{-1}_D\to g'^{-1}_Df^{-1}_D$ be the transformation on $D$ of [def-weil-pbc-derived-square-iso], with $\theta^D_{\mathrm{unb},QK}=\beta_{2,K}^{-1}\circ Q(\theta_{\square,K})\circ\beta_{1,K}$ for every complex $K$. Claim: $\psi_{QK}\circ\theta^D_{\mathrm{unb},(QK)[1]}=\theta^D_{\mathrm{unb},QK}[1]\circ\varphi_{QK}$. Since $h=f'^{-1}_Dg^{-1}_D(c_K):f'^{-1}_Dg^{-1}_D(Q(K[1]))\to f'^{-1}_Dg^{-1}_D((QK)[1])$ is an isomorphism it suffices to compare both sides after precomposing with $h$. Left: by naturality of $\theta^D_{\mathrm{unb}}$ for $c_K$, $\theta^D_{\mathrm{unb},(QK)[1]}\circ h=g'^{-1}_Df^{-1}_D(c_K)\circ\theta^D_{\mathrm{unb},Q(K[1])}$, and by Step 2 for $\beta_2$, $\psi_{QK}\circ g'^{-1}_Df^{-1}_D(c_K)=\beta_{2,K}[1]^{-1}\circ c_{g'^{-1}f^{-1}K}\circ\beta_{2,K[1]}$; so the left side is $\beta_{2,K}[1]^{-1}\circ c_{g'^{-1}f^{-1}K}\circ\beta_{2,K[1]}\circ\beta_{2,K[1]}^{-1}\circ Q(\theta_{\square,K[1]})\circ\beta_{1,K[1]}=\beta_{2,K}[1]^{-1}\circ c_{g'^{-1}f^{-1}K}\circ Q(\theta_{\square,K[1]})\circ\beta_{1,K[1]}$. By Step 3 this is $\beta_{2,K}[1]^{-1}\circ(Q\theta_{\square,K})[1]\circ c_{f'^{-1}g^{-1}K}\circ\beta_{1,K[1]}$, and by Step 2 for $\beta_1$, $c_{f'^{-1}g^{-1}K}\circ\beta_{1,K[1]}=\beta_{1,K}[1]\circ\varphi_{QK}\circ h$. So the left side is $(\beta_{2,K}^{-1}\circ Q\theta_{\square,K}\circ\beta_{1,K})[1]\circ\varphi_{QK}\circ h=\theta^D_{\mathrm{unb},QK}[1]\circ\varphi_{QK}\circ h$, the right side precomposed with $h$ ($[1]$ is a functor). Cancel the isomorphism $h$.

proof.text: **Step 5 (the square on all of $D$).** The two sides are the components at $X$ of two natural transformations $\sigma,\sigma'$ between the functors $G_1=f'^{-1}_D\circ g^{-1}_D\circ[1]$ and $G_2=[1]\circ g'^{-1}_D\circ f^{-1}_D$ from $D(Y_{\Et})$ to $D(X'_{\Et})$: $\sigma_X=\psi_X\circ\theta^D_{\mathrm{unb},X[1]}$ and $\sigma'_X=\theta^D_{\mathrm{unb},X}[1]\circ\varphi_X$, natural in $X$ as composites of natural transformations ($\psi,\varphi$ natural, $\theta^D_{\mathrm{unb}}$ natural, whiskered by $[1]$ on either side). By Step 4, $\sigma_{QK}=\sigma'_{QK}$ for every complex $K$. $Q$ is a localization at the quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], so by the uniqueness clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] (with $L=Q$, $\mathcal E=D(X'_{\Et})$), $\sigma=\sigma'$: $\psi_X\circ\theta^D_{\mathrm{unb},X[1]}=\theta^D_{\mathrm{unb},X}[1]\circ\varphi_X$ for every $X\in D(Y_{\Et})$. (Source: categories.tex Lemma 04VG (3): a functor out of $S^{-1}\mathcal C$ is determined by its composite with $Q$; Mathlib Localization.natTrans_ext.)

**Step 6 (restriction to $\Dplus$).** For $M\in\Dplus(Y_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]: $M[1]\in\Dplus(Y_{\Et})$ and the shift of $\Dplus$ is that of $D$; $\theta^D_{\square,M}=\theta^D_{\mathrm{unb},M}$ and $\theta^D_{\square,M[1]}=\theta^D_{\mathrm{unb},M[1]}$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-square-iso]; the inverse images on $\Dplus$ and their shift isomorphisms are the restrictions of those on $D$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image], [lem-weil-pbc-triangulated-functor-restriction], hence so are the composite isomorphisms $\varphi_M,\psi_M$ (Step 2's formulas, read in the full subcategory). So the identity of the statement at $M$ is the identity of Step 5 at $X=M$, read in the full subcategory $\Dplus(X'_{\Et})$.

proof.text: **Step 7 (iterates).** Define $\varphi^{(0)}=\mathrm{id}$, $\varphi^{(n+1)}_M=\varphi^{(n)}_M[1]\circ\varphi_{M[n]}$ for $n\ge0$ and $\varphi^{(-m)}_M=((\varphi^{(m)}_{M[-m]})^{-1})[-m]$, likewise $\psi^{(n)}$. Then $\psi^{(n)}_M\circ\theta^D_{\square,M[n]}=\theta^D_{\square,M}[n]\circ\varphi^{(n)}_M$ for all $n\in\mathbf Z$: for $n\ge0$ by induction, $\psi^{(n+1)}_M\circ\theta^D_{M[n+1]}=\psi^{(n)}_M[1]\circ\psi_{M[n]}\circ\theta^D_{M[n][1]}=\psi^{(n)}_M[1]\circ\theta^D_{M[n]}[1]\circ\varphi_{M[n]}=(\theta^D_M[n]\circ\varphi^{(n)}_M)[1]\circ\varphi_{M[n]}=\theta^D_M[n+1]\circ\varphi^{(n+1)}_M$ (Step 6 at $M[n]$, functoriality of $[1]$); for $n=-m<0$ the case $m$ at $M[-m]$, $\psi^{(m)}_{M[-m]}\circ\theta^D_M=\theta^D_{M[-m]}[m]\circ\varphi^{(m)}_{M[-m]}$, rearranges to $(\psi^{(m)}_{M[-m]})^{-1}\circ\theta^D_{M[-m]}[m]=\theta^D_M\circ(\varphi^{(m)}_{M[-m]})^{-1}$, and applying $[-m]$ (with $[m][-m]=\mathrm{id}$ on complexes) gives the claim. This is the induction written out for the exchange morphism by its user (the derived exchange lemma, Step 5); in Mathlib terms, NatTrans.CommShift for $\mathbf Z$ is determined by the case $a=1$.
